meta: Concept site for Red Clay & Fern Landscapes, a made-up Athens, Georgia landscaper: design, native planting, lawn care and drainage for clay soil. Designed by shash.builds.

hero.title: A yard you'll actually want to sit in.
hero.sub: Design, planting and year-round care for Athens and Oconee County homes, with plants that can take Georgia clay and August heat.

services_title: From bare clay to a finished yard.
services: A plan drawn for your yard, your light and how you actually use the space.
Trees, shrubs and perennials picked to thrive here, not just look good at the nursery.
Mowing, edging, aeration and overseeding on a schedule that fits the season.
Stone, brick and gravel work that ties the yard together.
French drains, dry creek beds and grading so rain stops pooling by the house.
Leaves, pruning, fresh mulch and bed edging, spring and fall.

extra.title: What we do, season by season.
items: New beds, fresh mulch, aeration and the first mow.
Mowing, watering checks and weed control through the heat.
Trees and shrubs, overseeding and leaf cleanup.
Pruning, design work and patio or path builds.

steps_title: How a new yard comes together.
steps: We walk the yard with you, check the soil and light, and ask how you want to use it.
You get a simple drawing and a written price within a week.
We build it, then keep it healthy with weekly or seasonal visits.

area.note: We keep our routes close so your crew isn't stuck in traffic between yards.

about.title: We learned on our own red clay.
body: Athens clay is hard in August and soup in March. Most plants from a big-box store don't make it through their first summer here.
We plant what works: natives and tough perennials that handle the heat, feed the pollinators and need less water once they're settled.

promise.title: Every plant we install is covered for a year.
promise.body: If a tree, shrub or perennial we planted dies within twelve months, we replace it. You just keep it watered.

faq: When is the best time to plant?
Fall. Roots grow through the mild winter, so plants are ready before the summer heat. Spring works too with more watering.
Can you work with our clay soil?
Yes. We amend beds with compost and pick plants that like clay, so you're not fighting it every year.
Yes, weekly or every other week from April to October, with edging and blowing included.
Can you fix water pooling by the house?
Usually. A French drain, a dry creek bed or regrading moves the water where it should go. We'll show you options on the yard walk.
How much does a design cost?
The yard walk and sketch are free. You get a written price for the full project before anything is planted.

form.title: Book a walk around your yard.
form.note: Tell us a little about the yard. We'll call to set a time that works, usually within the week.
